comment: Brian (ElevenLabs) VO for Episode 25 (300s): England vs Croatia, Group L, real kickoff 23:00 Wed 17 Jun 2026. VERIFIED real facts (cite in README): 11 July 2018, Luzhniki Stadium, Moscow — World Cup SEMI-FINAL. Kieran Trippier put England ahead with a 5th-minute free-kick ('It's Coming Home' at its loudest). Ivan Perisic equalised on 68'. In EXTRA TIME, the 109th minute, Mario Mandzukic scored the winner: Croatia 2-1 England (AET). Croatia — a nation of about 4 million — reached their first ever World Cup final, where they lost 4-2 to France. Luka Modric won the 2018 Golden Ball (player of the tournament), the first Croatian ever to do so. England's only World Cup win is 1966 — never since. Croatia's record for a tiny nation is astonishing: third in 1998 (debut), runners-up 2018, third again 2022. RULES: Ep24 PRT-COD recap labelled OUR PREDICTION (we predicted Portugal 3-1 DR Congo). This ending is OUR PREDICTION (England 2-1 Croatia). Soccer only — round-neck shirts, a pitch with goals, NO helmets/pads. Lines short — never tempo-stretch.

lines.text: Eight years ago, a nation of barely four million people walked out a goal down against a giant — and ended its dream.
Tonight, those two meet again. And somewhere in the stands, a figure in a red-and-white checkerboard is watching, and waiting.
Last time, we predicted Portugal would beat DR Congo three-one — the old kings against the rising Leopards. Tonight: the giant, against the ghost.
Welcome back to WorldCup twenty-six Legends, episode twenty-five. England versus Croatia. The empire... and the little nation that broke it.
And stay with me — because late in this one, the ghost of two thousand eighteen walks again.
First, the history. And this one is true. Moscow. The Luzhniki Stadium. The eleventh of July, two thousand eighteen — a World Cup semi-final.
After five minutes, Kieran Trippier bent in a free kick. England, one to nothing. And around the world, four words sang out: it's coming home.
But Croatia would not bow. On sixty-eight minutes, Ivan Perisic hooked it level. The giant started to wobble.
Extra time. The hundred-and-ninth minute. Mario Mandzukic. A nation of four million had broken England's heart — and reached their first World Cup final.
Their captain, Luka Modric, was named the best player of the whole tournament. And tonight, eight years on, the rematch.
But this England has grown up.
England. The Three Lions. World champions exactly once, in nineteen sixty-six — and aching, ever since, for one more.
Harry Kane. The captain. England's all-time leading scorer — a man chasing the one prize that has always escaped him.
Around him, Jude Bellingham, Bukayo Saka, Phil Foden — a midfield jewel and two wingers in their prime. This attack can hurt anyone.
The deepest squad on the planet. But across the line stands the team that has done the impossible before.
Croatia. The Vatreni. The greatest overachievers football has ever seen — three World Cup podiums from a country of under four million.
And still, at the heart of them, Luka Modric — the maestro, the Golden Ball, the man who simply will not stop running.
With Josko Gvardiol and Mateo Kovacic, steel front to back, and Andrej Kramaric, ice-cold in front of goal.
So here is the duel. England's depth against Croatia's scars. The giant who has everything to prove... against the ghost who's done it all before.
Our prediction — built on England's power, on Croatia's heart, and on one young king who refuses to lose. Watch.
England press first. A corner swings in, Saka whips it deep — and there is the captain. Harry Kane rises, and heads it home. One-nil.
But you do not frighten a nation that once broke this very team. Croatia steady, and Modric begins to pull the strings.
He slides it through, and the ice-man arrives. Andrej Kramaric, one touch, one finish — one-all. The ghost is breathing.
And just as Moscow flickers back — England's young king answers. Bellingham, driving, late, unstoppable. Two-one.
Two-one at the whistle, in our story. England lay the ghost of twenty-eighteen to rest — but Croatia, the tiny giants, made them earn every inch.
Do you agree? Comment THREE LIONS if England finally bury the past. Comment VATRENI if the little nation breaks them all over again.
And the figure in the checkerboard? Legend number twenty-five: the Ghost of twenty-eighteen.
He wears the shirt from that night in Moscow — when a country smaller than a single English city humbled a giant. Collect him inside the game.
Which brings us to YOU. At WorldCup twenty-six dot world, pick three of the forty-eight nations — and every goal they score... scores for you.
Free to play. Climb the leaderboard, just for fun. No prizes.
Hit like — send this to the friend who still thinks football is only about the big nations. And subscribe: the legends are only beginning.
